---
title: "Monotonic Stack: Each Item Is Pushed and Popped Once"
description: "A mathematical interview pattern explained by a small example and proof."
---

## Recognition trigger

Next greater element, histogram bounds and nearest smaller neighbour.

## Main question

**Why is the while-loop work linear even if many elements are popped at once?**

## Formula worth memorising

$$
\#push+\#pop\le2n
$$

**Every symbol explained:** #push counts pushes of input elements onto a stack; #pop counts removals of those elements; n is number of input positions. The bound assumes each element enters at most once and is removed at most once.

**Substitute actual numbers:** Scan [2,1,3] while keeping a decreasing stack for next-greater searches: push 2, push 1; when 3 arrives, pop 1 and 2, then push 3. Total pushes=3, pops=2: 5≤2×3=6.

## Derivation and correctness reasoning

Each input index is pushed once and, after being popped, never re-enters. Charge each pop to its unique earlier push. Total stack operations are at most 2n even though pops appear inside a nested loop.

## Failure modes and assumptions

Stack comparison direction matters: greater versus greater-or-equal changes answers when duplicate values occur. State the equality policy in the invariant.

## The 20-second memory card

**Memorise: Maintain monotonic order; every pop is permanent, so total pushes and pops are O(n).**

Practise reciting the invariant or proof, not merely the equation.

**Interview problems:** Daily Temperatures; Next Greater Element.
